title: Logo vs Wordmark Registration for New Businesses in Kattakada
metaTitle: Wordmark vs Logo Trademark in Kattakada | BRNDNUR Advisory
metaDescription: Understand whether to file a wordmark, device mark, or composite logo for your new business in Kattakada. Strategic analysis of protection scopes.
intendedAudience: New shop owners, manufacturing entrepreneurs, and service founders in Kattakada, Malayinkeezhu, and Poovachal.
quickAnswer: A wordmark protects the brand name itself in plain text regardless of font, color, or design styling, providing the broadest commercial monopoly. A logo (device mark) protects only the specific visual graphic, typography, or emblem as filed. For new ventures in Kattakada, filing a wordmark first is strongly recommended, followed by a logo trademark as visual brand identity matures.

h2Sections.h2: The Core Strategic Distinction: Text vs Graphic
content: When preparing Form TM-A on the IP India portal, applicants must declare the "Category of Mark." The two most common choices are Word Mark and Device Mark. Understanding the legal difference is vital to avoid leaving critical brand assets unprotected.

Entrepreneurs in Kattakada often spend money designing a logo and mistakenly assume registering that specific graphic protects the name itself in any format. In reality, a competitor might copy your name using a different font or color if you have only protected a specific graphic mark.

h2Sections.h2: Comparison: Wordmark vs. Device / Logo Mark
content: Here is how the legal rights and commercial protections compare under the Trade Marks Act, 1999:

rows: The alphabetical letters and text itself.
The exact visual emblem, design, typography, and color arrangement.
Broadest monopoly: protects the word in ANY font, size, casing, or styling.
Narrower monopoly: protects ONLY the specific graphic design submitted in Form TM-A.
Zero impact: you can completely re-design your logo without affecting your registration.
High impact: major logo redesigns require filing a fresh trademark application.
Recommended first filing for maximum trade protection.
Recommended second filing for distinctive graphic emblems and packaging badges.

h2Sections.h2: When Should a Kattakada Business File Both?
content: If your brand features a highly recognizable standalone visual icon—such as a crest on packaged goods or a stylized character—filing both marks offers complete legal perimeter defense:
1. The wordmark prevents rivals from launching products using your name.
2. The device mark prevents rivals from using similar visual symbols with a different name to create customer confusion.

faqs.question: Can I file a word and logo together in one application?
faqs.answer: Yes, this is known as a "Composite Mark." However, if you later modify the logo artwork or font, the legal protection over the composite mark becomes diluted, which is why separate filings are preferred for core brand assets.

faqs.question: Which is cheaper to file: wordmark or logo?
faqs.answer: The official government fee is identical: ₹4,500 per class for individuals and MSMEs, or ₹9,000 per class for other corporate entities.
